To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the classical univariate method (two-sample t-test) is unrobust in the existence of noisy (or wrong) training labels; (2) stability selection is robust in existence of noisy training labels; (3) the elastic net method is robust in existence data variation; (4) our proposed feature selection method is robust in both existence of noisy training label and existence of data variation.

(1) the stability selection method can improve the reliability of feature selection, and (2) the elastic net method is able to select the redundant but informative biomarkers, which is important for both the potential biomarker discovery and the robustness of classifier.

the proposed method is able to provide a more stable and robust selection of informative redundant features and a better interpretability of discovered potential biomarkers in case of high dimensional fMRI data, and the stability selection approach can be successfully used for feature selection in the field of neuroimaging.

the problem of feature selection in high dimensional fMRI data and our proposed approach is expected to be useful for future researches on the fMRI data.

a novel approach for stable selection of redundant but informative features from high dimensional fMRI data.

our method can provide a more reliable and interpretable potential biomarker for ADHD diagnosis.

the stability selection approach can help to select stable features, and that the elastic net approach can help to improve the interpretability of the selected features.
